changes.finding: C07 aggregate PID count does not establish per-root coverage
changes.before: Each command must settle within 5 s; shared PID log must include every expected started root and all recorded fixture processes must be dead afterward.
changes.after: Each command must settle within 5 s; the shared log must satisfy pids.len() >= started, an aggregate lower bound on complete PID entries. That count does not identify every expected root individually; assert_dead_logged subsequently checks the PIDs actually recorded.
changes.reason: pids_in parses complete newline-terminated PID entries. The test compares their aggregate count to the number of non-pre-cancelled command kinds; it does not map entries to every expected root. Descendant entries can contribute to that aggregate. It subsequently calls assert_dead_logged on the recorded PID vector. The five-second per-command timeout remains unchanged.

changes.finding: C07 large environment size versus comment rationale and unobserved fallback
changes.before: Sends a 64 KiB OMNI_BIG value, exceeding the socket-buffer scale while staying below Linux single-env-string limits.
changes.after: Sets OMNI_BIG to 64 KiB of x; the source comment compares that size with an 8 KiB socket buffer and Linux's 128 KiB limit for one environment string. This test does not measure/configure socket capacity or establish that EMSGSIZE or its fallback branch occurred.
changes.reason: The fixture input is explicitly 64 * 1024 x characters. The 8 KiB socket-buffer and Linux 128 KiB comparisons occur in a source comment. The complete 29-line source has no socket-capacity measurement/configuration or assertion that EMSGSIZE or its fallback branch was reached.

changes.finding: C07 actual output assertions and configured timeout
changes.before: Requires successful fixture execution and exact printed value framing/length under a 30 s timeout.
changes.after: Configures a 30 s command timeout and requires successful exit, text.starts_with("OMNI_BIG=\"xxx"), and text.trim_end().len() == big.len() + 11; the assertions do not compare the complete returned value or validate full framing.
changes.reason: The command is configured with a 30-second timeout. After run returns, the source asserts successful exit, the shown prefix, and text.trim_end().len() == big.len() + 11. Those conditions do not compare the full value or establish complete framing. The method is trim_end, not trim; these remain unexecuted source assertions.
